policy_title: Reduce Corporation Tax and raise profit threshold
stated: Reform UK will free over 1.2 million Small and Medium Sized Businesses (SMEs) from Corporation Tax by lifting the minimum profit threshold to £100,000, and reduce the main Corporation Tax rate from 25% to 20%, then to 15% from Year 3.

source.quote: Free Over 1.2 Million Small and Medium Sized Businesses from Corporation Tax Lift the minimum profit threshold to £100k. Reduce the main Corporation Tax Rate from 25% to 20%, then to 15% from Year 3.

bearing_set.reason: Reducing corporation tax and lifting the profit threshold directly affects SME economics — investment capacity, hiring decisions, wage offers, and job creation — for businesses that collectively employ the majority of UK private-sector workers.
Directly reduces the corporation tax burden on SME owners and shareholders, increasing retained/distributable profits and effective take-home for business owners.

Cutting the main rate from 25% to 15% and exempting ~1.2m businesses from CT materially reduces a major revenue stream (CT raised ~£85bn in 2023/24), worsening the funded/borrowed balance unless growth fully offsets the loss.

Lower CT is a classical supply-side lever intended to raise business investment, productivity and firm formation; the effect on aggregate living standards is real but contested (depends on how much of the cut is invested vs distributed and whether the fiscal drag constrains public investment).

Corporation tax incidence falls predominantly on capital owners and shareholders, who are concentrated in higher-income deciles; a large cut (25%→15%) plausibly widens the income/wealth gap, a concrete distributional mechanism assessable via IFS-style incidence analysis.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: a direct tax-burden benefit (O11), a substantial fiscal cost (O12), a contested supply-side growth effect (O13), and a distributional/inequality spillover (O14). Other fundamentals (O3, O4, O6, etc.) are either too indirect or lack a pinnable indicator movement.
